privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.summary: Hush processes extension data locally on your device. It does not upload, sell, share, or transmit this data to Hush or any third party.

data.title: Data processed locally
data.intro: Hush may store the following data in chrome.storage.local:
items: Domains, full URLs, and CSS selectors that you choose to mark.
Search queries, search engine names, and timestamps when search history is enabled.
Marking statistics, preferences, language selection, ad-marking settings, and subdomain-matching settings.
The same local data when you explicitly export a Hush backup file.
data.outro: Search history can be disabled at any time and existing history can be deleted from the extension settings.

processing.title: Search page processing
processing.description: On the explicitly supported Google, Baidu, Bing, 360 Search, Sogou, Yahoo!, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo domains, Hush reads DOM structure, visible advertising labels, and result links to identify and mark search results. This processing happens entirely inside your browser. Page content and search queries are not transmitted.
processing.scope: Hush does not inject or scan pages outside the exact supported search-engine domains declared in the extension Manifest.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.storage: Saves rules, search history, statistics, backups, and preferences locally.
permissions.contextMenus: Adds actions to block domains, block links, and pick page elements to the browser context menu.
permissions.hostDescription: Runs the result-marking Content Script only on the declared Google, Baidu, Bing, 360 Search, Sogou, Yahoo!, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo domains.

entries.title: Initial release
items: Mark an entire domain or only one specific URL from a search result.
Select page elements visually and create site-scoped CSS selector rules.
Choose whether domain rules also apply to subdomains.
Display a clear badge over marked results and restore them directly from the page.
Detect and mark advertising and sponsored results with an independent settings toggle.
Support Google, Baidu, Bing, 360 Search, Sogou, Yahoo!, Yandex, and DuckDuckGo out of the box.
Automatically detect result structures on supported search pages as their layouts change.
Keep marking active across dynamically loaded results and search-page navigation.
Quickly block domains, full links, or selected page elements from the browser's native context menu.
Optionally save search history and clear individual records or the full history at any time.
Show marking statistics in the dashboard and the current page count in the browser tab badge.
Store all rules and preferences locally, with JSON backup and restore support.
Provide English and Simplified Chinese interfaces with runtime language switching.
